name: fur
summary: A pelt: an animal's coat, matted and dull, with the strands painted into the sheet and nothing added to them.
why: This exists because hair is not fur, and the Bull Fighter proved it. hair.json is a bare
head: a small patch, brushed along v at scale 260 so the sheen does not lie flat across the
crown. Put on a whole animal it draws that grain across the entire atlas, and on a body
whose sheets are stretched ten thousand units across the model the strands come out as
evenly spaced ridges running the length of the back and the thighs - a striped bull,
reported three times from screenshots before the material was found under it.
No grain at all. MU paints the pelt as a mottled brown-black with the strand shading
already in it - npc_a_01 and 02 carry a dark band of drawn hairs - and at 64 pixels a
sheet there is nothing a procedural strand could reconstruct that the paint has not drawn.
The three grain kinds are facts about how a surface was made, and fur was not made.
Roughness 0.78, skin's, and above hair's 0.62 on purpose: a coat catches no directional
sheen at the size a monster is seen, and hair's gloss was the other half of the stripes -
each ridge caught the sun along its length. Metallic 0.0, as everything on a body.
